Metaphysica admittit ut in Physica; scien-
tiarum multitudinem non item. Scientiæ
enim non sunt multiplicandæ secundum
genera & species (aliâs namque Physica
constaret tot scientiis quot partibus, alia
esset scientia quæ de Corpore loqueretur,
alia quæ de Cœlo, alia quæ de Elementis)
sed secundum modum considerandi: atqui
modus considerandi in Metaphysica unus
& idem est, quicquid enim illa considerat,
debet à materia sejunctum esse.
XII. Hactenus de Objecto. Genus
Metaphysicæ est Scientia, idque stricta ra-

page.notes: The Greek passages are only partly legible at this scan resolution. The words marked [?] are best readings, and the stretch between "ποιήσει" and "ἀλλὰ" is not read reliably, so it is shown with an ellipsis-like gap. The phrase "nec versatur" is followed by Greek that could not be fully copied. The word "miftis" is as printed. The catchword "bus" is at the foot and is not repeated in the text; the paragraph ends on the hyphenated "qui-" because the next page continues the word. The faint digitiser mark at the lower right was omitted.
